title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_0RD0RC_1LE1LF_1LD---_0LB1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_0RD0RC_1LE1LF_1LD---_0LB1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the shift rules of a sweep and the only halting shape (1 D> 0). In 109 steps D read a 0 66,714,267 times, always with a 0 to its left. The phase structure is observed, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,052 cells have been visited and 22,709 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.111). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: Leftward, D and E turn (00)^n into (11)^n, then A and F turn (11)^n into (10)^n, 2 steps a pair; rightward, a zigzag from 0 0 D> turns (10)^n back into (11)^n, 10 steps a pair; B crosses ones unchanged and C turns them into zeros.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: E on a 1 halts; E is entered only from D on a 0 (1LE). D comes from C on a 0 moving right (C wrote a 0 where E would land) or from E on a 0 moving left. So it halts iff D reads a 0 with a 1 to its left: 1 D> 0 puts E on that 1 (the converse by reading the table, not formalized).

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In 109 steps D reads a 0 66,714,267 times; the cell to its left is always 0. E reads a 0 about 6.67·107 times, never with 1 0 (nearest first 0 1) to its left.

claims.title: Sweeps and phases
claims.text: Sampled with C on a 0 at the right end (once a sweep), the tape is a short counter followed by 1^K 0^Z. One sweep (about 4.6 times the tape length in steps) takes K down by 1 or 3 and Z up by 4 while the counter on the left ticks. When K is used up a new phase starts with K about the whole tape: phases began near steps 5.8·105, 2.3·106, 9.4·106, 3.8·107, 1.5·108, 6.0·108 with tape lengths 838, 1678, 3358, 6718, 13446, 26894.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs 1 D> 0, which the sweeps never produce; it would have to come from the counter on the left or from the change of phase, whose rules have not been worked out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 32,052 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Phases last about 4 times longer each.

sections.heading: Rewriting the right part, back and forth
html: At step 16,085,367 the tape (as runs) is 11 0^6 111 0^8 1^21 0^7 1^2670 0^1377 with C on a 0 at the right end. Going left, D and E fill the zeros with ones, then A and F turn the big block of ones into (10)^1334. Near the left the head turns, and a slow zigzag (10 steps a pair) turns the (10) back into ones; then C, crossing the ones that were zeros, turns them back into zeros. After 18,762 steps the tape is ... 1^21 0^6 1^2669 0^1381: the block of ones lost one cell, the zeros gained four. All these passes are shift rules proved in Lean.

sections.heading: A tape that doubles
html: The short counter on the left (21/7, 21/6, 21/2 2/3, 21/2 2/2, 22/7, ...) ticks once a sweep and decides whether the block of ones loses 1 or 3 cells. When the block is gone, the zeros become the new block and a new phase starts. The tape length at the starts of the phases is
about doubling, at steps about four times apart (5.8·105 to 6.0·108).

sections.heading: Never a 1 behind D
html: E reading a 1 halts. Working backwards through the table, the only way there is D reading a 0 with a 1 just to its left (Lean: halt_shape). D reads a 0 in every leftward pass over the zeros, but the cell to its left is then still a 0: in 109 steps it read a 0 66.7 million times, always with a 0 on its left.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.111). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,052 cells (120 left of the start, 24,496 right), with a density of 1s of 0.709.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer that rewrites the right part of the tape on every sweep (ones to (10), back to ones, zeros to ones and back), while a short counter on the left ticks; the tape length roughly doubles each phase and each phase lasts about four times longer.
family: bouncer with a doubling tape (phases about 4 times longer each)
